rejectedAlternatives.reason: Synchronous audit writers and authorization queries cross Identity, Organizations, Teams, Projects, Boards, Workflows and WorkItems.
Largest domain and integration surface; owns board, sprint, search, realtime, upload, webhook and reporting effects.

http.rollback: Set Gateway:NotificationExtractionEnabled=false and restart/reload the gateway; the existing /api/{**catch-all} route returns ownership to the monolith.

data.ownershipRule: Exactly one notification writer topology is active at a time; no dual write.
data.privacyBoundary: Identity privacy export/anonymization must call a versioned notification privacy port after process extraction; direct repository access is transitional monolith coupling.

synchronousDependencies.purpose: Resolve active user, organization and email without sharing the Identity repository.
Non-idempotent external email delivery with durable notification retry/dead-letter ownership.
Deduplication and notification delivery lease coordination.
Export and anonymize notification references under the existing privacy workflow.

migration: Keep the default gateway route and all notification writes in the monolith.
Publish the two producer-owned V1 events through an outbox relay and consume with an extracted-service inbox using the existing consumer and deduplication identities.
Run the extracted process against the same logical Notifications store with exclusive worker leases; compare reads, counts, indexes and delivery metrics while HTTP routing remains on the monolith.
Move the Notifications store by snapshot plus ordered change catch-up; pause notification mutations for the final high-watermark and never dual-write.
Enable the notification-specific gateway route only after readiness, privacy, inbox lag and data parity gates pass.
During the rollback window retain the monolith code and a reverse change journal; freeze extracted writes, apply the bounded reverse delta, disable the route flag and resume the monolith worker.
rollbackGates: Extracted worker and HTTP writers are stopped or fenced before the monolith resumes.
Notification/preference counts, deduplication keys, unread state and email lease/status deltas reconcile at one high-watermark.
Outbox relay offsets and service inbox deduplication identities are retained; messages are replayed, not regenerated.
Gateway readiness is healthy after the route flag is disabled.
No notification is delivered twice and no preference mutation is lost.
